name: Lootbox (jx-codes/lootbox)
pinned: 587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a (deno.json version 0.0.54, last commit 2026-02-27); run from source on host Deno 2.9.8 with --no-lock (see surprises)
engine: A fresh `deno run --allow-net --allow-import=localhost:<port>` subprocess per script (V8 + Deno permissions; local script is type-checked). Tools are .ts files in .lootbox/tools, each run in a long-lived `deno run --allow-all` worker process; scripts reach them over a WebSocket to the lootbox server.
how_run: `deno run --allow-all --no-lock src/lootbox-cli.ts server` in research/probes/lootbox/work (lootbox.config.json: port 41310, root .lootbox, data ./data); `lookup` is .lootbox/tools/host.ts; each probe is sent as the same WebSocket message `lootbox exec` sends ({script, id}). Sandbox code calls tools.host.lookup(...).

P1.detail: printed 42, 1 host call (counted by the tool worker in work/calls.log). First execution 2,366 ms including client download and type check.

P2.detail: Only stdout returns, as `result`: 200,001 chars (all 200,000 A's), no truncation, no marker. The bare last expression "RETURNED" is not returned (module file, no return channel).

P3.detail: fetch("https://example.com") returned 200 with a 577-char body. User scripts run with unrestricted --allow-net by design; there is no option to turn it off.

P4.detail: require -> ReferenceError: require is not defined; node:fs readFileSync and Deno.readTextFile -> NotCapable: Requires read access to "/etc/hosts".

P5.detail: process.env.PROBE_SECRET and Deno.env.get -> NotCapable: Requires env access to "PROBE_SECRET". The subprocess inherits the full server env (no env option on Deno.Command); only the missing --allow-env hides it.

P6.detail: Killed after 10,073 ms by the hard-coded 10 s AbortController. The caller gets error = only Deno's "Download ... / Check ..." stderr lines with no timeout message: the "Script execution timeout (10 seconds)" branch never runs because Deno's output() resolves on abort instead of throwing.

P7.detail: No memory limit. Harness killed the script process at 4,314 MB process-tree RSS after 6.8 s (before the 10 s timeout fired). Server survived; next execution printed alive.

P8.detail: fresh. The spec form `globalThis.kept = 7` fails type checking (TS7017), so the equivalent `(globalThis as any).kept = 7` was used; the second run printed gone.

P9.detail: 327 ms measured inside the script for 5 Promise.all lookups, 5 host calls: parallel (the extra ~120 ms is two WebSocket hops per call).

P10.detail: error = raw Deno stderr with ANSI codes: "Download http://localhost:41310/client.ts?v=1", "Check file:///var/folders/.../T/<random>.ts", "error: Uncaught (in promise) Error: probe-boom", source line, caret, "at file:///...ts:<line>:7". Message and line survive; line numbers are user line + 3 (injected import). Anything printed before the throw is dropped (X3).

P11.detail: median 591.5 ms, p90 844 ms per execution: each run spawns deno, re-downloads client.ts (--reload) and type-checks the script. One-time setup 7,551 ms (server start, tool worker start, type generation).

P12.detail: Spec forms fail type checking (TS2532, TS2683). With // @ts-ignore: this.constructor -> TypeError (module this is undefined); (function(){return this})().process -> TypeError. globalThis.process is the script's own Deno process: env read NotCapable; Deno.Command("echo") -> NotCapable run access; node:child_process execSync -> NotCapable. No host object reached.

defaults.time: 10 s per script, hard-coded (src/lib/execute_llm_script.ts:26); not configurable. Tool calls time out at 30 s (src/lib/rpc/client.ts:26, rpc_worker.ts:69). The CLI waits 30 s for a response. No stricter option exists, so hardened is null.
defaults.memory: None. P7 reached 4.3 GB before the harness stopped it.
defaults.output: None. stdout returned whole on success; on failure only stderr (stdout dropped).
defaults.tool_calls: No count cap. Network is always on (--allow-net with no host list) and there is no config key for it.

source_notes.finding: Each .ts file in .lootbox/tools is a namespace and its exported functions become tools. The server extracts their TypeScript types and generates a client module (`export const tools = { <ns>: { <fn>: createRpcCall("ns.fn") } }`) served at /client.ts; every script gets `import { tools } from "http://localhost:<port>/client.ts?v=<n>"` prepended. MCP servers appear as mcp_<name> namespaces.

On demand through the CLI: `lootbox tools` lists namespaces, `lootbox tools types <ns,...>` fetches TypeScript for chosen namespaces from /types/:namespaces. The agent pulls only what it needs, which scales past 100 tools.

The script opens a WebSocket to the lootbox server and sends {method: "ns.fn", args, id}; the server routes it to that namespace's worker process over /worker-ws. Tool workers run with --allow-all, so a tool has full host access by design.

Scripts run as `deno run --allow-net --allow-import=localhost:<port> --reload=... --no-check=remote <tmp>.ts`. Files, env and subprocesses are denied by Deno permissions; network is fully open. Help text says 'Sandboxed execution keeps your system safe' and 'Direct file system and environment access disabled', which matches; it also advertises fetch() as a feature. Open network means sandbox code can reach any LAN or localhost service, including the lootbox server itself (X1 fetched /client.ts, X2 started a nested script over /ws).

On success the response carries stdout as `result` (stderr warnings are dropped by the router). On failure it carries only stderr as `error`; stdout printed before the failure is discarded. No truncation anywhere.
10 s hard-coded wall clock via AbortController on Deno.Command; the timeout error branch is unreachable in practice (P6). No memory, output or call-count limits.

Fresh process per script. Persistent state lives in tools (example kv, sqlite, memory tools write to disk). Every script, its output and error are also stored in a SQLite history (lootbox.db in the data dir, default ~/.local/share/lootbox).

No formatting: the model sees Deno's raw stderr, including Download/Check progress lines, ANSI codes and the temp path. The local script is type-checked in strict mode, so a type error blocks execution before any code runs (P8 and P12 spec forms).
The server uses Deno.serve with no hostname, which listens on all interfaces, and /ws has no authentication: anyone who can reach the port can run scripts, and those scripts have open network.

surprises: The documented install (`deno install` then `deno task compile`, per install.sh) fails on Deno 2.9.8: deno.lock pins npm tarballs from registry.npmmirror.com, which Deno rejects as not matching registry.npmjs.org. The harness ran from source with --no-lock.

The timeout message 'Script execution timeout (10 seconds)' never reaches the caller: the aborted process resolves output() with success:false, so the caller gets only Deno's Download/Check stderr lines (P6).
Printed output is lost whenever a script fails: the router returns only stderr as error (X3).

Network is unrestricted by design (P3 works). The help text calls this 'Sandboxed execution keeps your system safe' while also allowing fetch to any host, including localhost services and the lootbox server itself (X1, X2).
Each execution costs about 0.6 s because the script is type-checked and client.ts is re-downloaded with --reload every time.
The spec's plain-JS probes fail TypeScript strict checking (TS7017, TS2532, TS2683), so model-written code that a JS sandbox would run can be rejected here before execution.
Every script and its output are persisted to a SQLite history in the user's home data dir by default, which matters for code that handles sensitive data.
